subject: math
title: Area of Parallelograms, Triangles, Trapezoids, Kites and Composite Polygons
seo_title: Grade 6 Area of Polygons Worksheets: Parallelograms, Triangles and Composite Shapes (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: Use the area relationships among rectangles, parallelograms, and triangles to develop the formulas for the area of a parallelogram and the area of a triangle, and solve related problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on area for the Ontario curriculum: parallelograms (A = b × h), triangles (A = ½ × b × h), trapezoids, rhombuses and kites split into triangles, composite polygons, and word problems about gardens, sails and flags. 100 questions with an answer key, good EQAO practice.
key_big: Parallelogram: A = b × h. Triangle: A = ½ × b × h.
key_sub: The height meets the base at a right angle; a slanted side is not the height. A triangle is half of a parallelogram with the same base and height. Split trapezoids, kites and other polygons into rectangles and triangles, then add. Area is in square units (cm², m²).
body_html:
The big idea: start from the rectangle

You know the area of a rectangle: base × height. Every shape in this unit can be cut apart, or doubled, to make a rectangle. The height is always measured at a right angle to the base. It is shown as a dashed line with a small square at the corner.

Parallelograms: A = b × h

Cut the triangle off one end and slide it to the other end. The parallelogram becomes a rectangle with the same base and the same height. A rhombus is a parallelogram too.

Triangles: A = 12 × b × h

Two copies of any triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height, so a triangle is half of it. In a right triangle, the two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height.

In a triangle with an obtuse angle, the height can fall outside the triangle. Extend the base with a dashed line and measure the height to that line.

Trapezoids and kites: cut them up

Cut a trapezoid into a rectangle and triangles, or into two triangles with a diagonal. Find each area and add.

A diagonal cuts a kite (or a rhombus) into two triangles that share it as their base. A kite fills exactly half of the rectangle drawn around it, so A = 12 × diagonal × diagonal.

Example

A trapezoid has parallel sides of 9 m and 5 m. They are 4 m apart. Find the area.

Cut it with a diagonal into two triangles. 12 × 9 × 4 = 18 and 12 × 5 × 4 = 10. Add: 18 + 10 = 28.

Answer: 28 m²

Composite polygons: split or subtract

Split the figure into rectangles and triangles that do not overlap, then add their areas. Or start with a big rectangle and subtract the piece that is missing.

Subtract a piece

A 10 m by 8 m rectangle has a triangle cut out. The triangle has a base of 8 m and a height of 3 m. Find the area left.

Rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80. Triangle: 12 × 8 × 3 = 12. Subtract: 80 − 12 = 68.

Answer: 68 m²

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the slanted side as the heightUse the dashed height at a right angle to the base
Triangle: 14 × 12 = 168Take half: 12 × 14 × 12 = 84
Parallelogram: 12 × 12 × 8 = 48No half for a parallelogram: 12 × 8 = 96
Kite: 12 × 13 = 156Take half: 12 × 12 × 13 = 78
Counting a corner twice in an L-shapeSplit into pieces that do not overlap
Writing 84 m for an areaArea is in square units: 84 m²

faq.q: What do Grade 6 students learn about area in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: In Grade 6 (Spatial Sense), students use rectangles to develop the formulas for the area of a parallelogram (A = b × h) and a triangle (A = ½ × b × h), and solve problems with them, including shapes they can split into rectangles and triangles.

faq.q: Why do you divide by 2 to find the area of a triangle?
faq.a: Two copies of the same triangle fit together to make a parallelogram with the same base and height. The triangle is half of it, so its area is ½ × base × height.

faq.q: How do you find the area of a trapezoid or a kite in Grade 6?
faq.a: Cut it into shapes you know. A trapezoid splits into a rectangle and triangles, or into two triangles with a diagonal. A kite splits into two triangles, so its area is ½ × one diagonal × the other.

faq.q: Is area on the Grade 6 EQAO math assessment?
faq.a: Yes. The Grade 6 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, and Spatial Sense, which includes area of parallelograms, triangles and composite shapes, is one of the strands it covers.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 11 × 15 = 165 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 17 m side.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 8 = 112 mm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 mm side.

items.q: A rectangle is 9 cm by 6 cm. A parallelogram has a base of 9 cm, a height of 6 cm and slanted sides of 7.5 cm. How do their areas compare?
c: The parallelogram is half as large.
items.e: Rectangle: 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Parallelogram: base × height = 9 × 6 = 54 cm². Same base and same height give the same area. (9 × 7.5 = 67.5 uses the slanted side.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 16 × 12 = 192 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 15 cm side.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 8.5 m and a height of 6 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 8.5 × 6 = 51 m². No 12 here: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 14 cm and a height of 11.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 14 × 11.5 = 161 cm². No 12 here: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 18 × 9 = 162 m². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 15 m side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 18 by 9.)

items.q: This rhombus has four sides of 15 m. What is its area?
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so A = base × height = 15 × 12 = 180 m². 15 × 15 uses a slanted side, not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 cm side.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 96 m². Its base is 12 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 12 × ? = 96. 96 ÷ 12 = 8 m. Check: 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × height = 15 × 12 = 180 m². 13 is the slanted side, 12 is for triangles, and 2 × (15 + 13) is the perimeter.

items.q: Cut along the dashed height and slide the triangle to the other end of the parallelogram. What rectangle do you get?
items.e: The base stays 10 m and the height stays 12 m, so the rectangle is 10 m by 12 m. That is why the parallelogram’s area is b × h = 10 × 12 = 120 m².

items.q: Cut along the dashed height and slide the triangle to the other end of the parallelogram. What rectangle do you get?
items.e: The base stays 14 cm and the height stays 8 cm, so the rectangle is 14 cm by 8 cm. That is why the parallelogram’s area is b × h = 14 × 8 = 112 cm².

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: Area = base × height = 11 × 12 = 132 cm². 15 is the slanted side, 12 is for triangles, and 2 × (11 + 15) is the perimeter.

items.q: A parallelogram has a base of 7.5 m and a height of 4.2 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 7.5 × 4.2 = 31.5 m². No 12 here: a parallelogram is a rectangle with one end cut off and moved.

items.q: A parallelogram has an area of 135 cm². Its height is 9 cm. How long is its base?
items.e: Area = base × height, so ? × 9 = 135. 135 ÷ 9 = 15 cm. Check: 15 × 9 = 135.

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 15 × 6 = 90 mm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 10 mm side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 15 by 6.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 15 × 16 = 240 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 20 cm side. (Cut off the triangle at one end and slide it to the other end: you get a rectangle that is 15 by 16.)

items.q: What is the area of the parallelogram?
items.e: A = base × height = 9 × 3 = 27 cm². The height is the dashed line at a right angle to the base, not the slanted 5 cm side.

items.q: This rhombus has four sides of 13 mm. What is its area?
items.e: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so A = base × height = 13 × 12 = 156 mm². 13 × 13 uses a slanted side, not the height.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 7.5 m and a height of 4 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = 12 × 7.5 × 4 = 12 × 30 = 15 m². Do not forget the 12: a triangle is half of a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = 12 × base × height = 12 × 15 × 10 = 12 × 150 = 75 mm². The 12.5 mm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 14 × 8 = 112 mm². The shaded triangle is half of it: 112 ÷ 2 = 56 mm².

items.q: A parallelogram and a triangle have the same base (14 cm) and the same height (9 cm). The parallelogram’s area is 126 cm². What is the triangle’s area?
items.e: Two copies of the triangle make a parallelogram with the same base and height, so the triangle is half of it: 126 ÷ 2 = 63 cm². Check: 12 × 14 × 9 = 12 × 126 = 63.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 4 cm. The height is the dashed 12 cm line, which meets the base line at a right angle outside the triangle. A = 12 × 4 × 12 = 24 cm².

items.q: A triangle has a base of 15 cm and a height of 8.4 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = 12 × 15 × 8.4 = 12 × 126 = 63 cm². Do not forget the 12: a triangle is half of a parallelogram.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = 12 × base × height = 12 × 8 × 3 = 12 × 24 = 12 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = 12 × base × height = 12 × 11 × 12 = 12 × 132 = 66 m². The 20 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height falls outside it and meets the grey dashed extension of the base.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 8 × 6 = 12 × 48 = 24 mm². The 10 mm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = 12 × base × height = 12 × 7 × 12 = 12 × 84 = 42 cm². The 20 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height falls outside it and meets the grey dashed extension of the base.

items.q: A triangle has an area of 42 m². Its height is 7 m. What is its base?
items.e: 12 × 7 × ? = 42. Double the area first: 42 × 2 = 84. Then 84 ÷ 7 = 12 m. Check: 12 × 7 × 12 = 12 × 84 = 42 m².

items.q: A triangle has an area of 36 cm². Its base is 9 cm. What is its height?
items.e: 12 × 9 × ? = 36. Double the area first: 36 × 2 = 72. Then 72 ÷ 9 = 8 cm. Check: 12 × 9 × 8 = 12 × 72 = 36 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 20 × 15 = 12 × 300 = 150 m². The 25 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 8 × 15 = 12 × 120 = 60 cm². The 17 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = 12 × base × height = 12 × 8 × 21 = 12 × 168 = 84 m². The 35 m side is slanted, so it is not the height. This triangle has an obtuse angle, so its height falls outside it and meets the grey dashed extension of the base.

items.q: A triangle has a base of 12 cm and a height of 6.5 cm. What is its area?
items.e: A = 12 × 12 × 6.5 = 12 × 78 = 39 cm². Do not forget the 12: a triangle is half of a parallelogram.

items.q: A diagonal cuts this rectangle into two equal triangles. What is the area of the shaded triangle?
items.e: The rectangle is 10 × 8 = 80 m². The shaded triangle is half of it: 80 ÷ 2 = 40 m².

items.q: What is the area of the triangle?
items.e: The height is the dashed line: it meets the base at a right angle. A = 12 × base × height = 12 × 7 × 6 = 12 × 42 = 21 cm². The 6.5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: What is the area of the right triangle?
items.e: The two sides that meet at the right angle are the base and the height. A = 12 × 3 × 4 = 12 × 12 = 6 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the triangle?
items.e: The base is 22 m. The height is the dashed 24 m line, which meets the base line at a right angle outside the triangle. A = 12 × 22 × 24 = 264 m².

sets.title: Trapezoids, rhombuses and kites: split into triangles and rectangles

items.q: What is the area of the rhombus?
items.e: The diagonals cut the rhombus into 4 equal right triangles. It fills half of the 10 by 14 rectangle around it: 12 × 10 × 14 = 12 × 140 = 70 m².

items.q: The horizontal diagonal cuts the kite into two triangles. What is the area of the kite?
items.e: Both triangles have the 15 m diagonal as their base. Top: 12 × 15 × 7 = 12 × 105 = 52.5 m². Bottom: 12 × 15 × 14 = 12 × 210 = 105 m². Add: 52.5 + 105 = 157.5 m².

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 8 = 48 m². The two triangles have the same height (8 m), and their bases add up to 18 − 6 = 12 m. Together: 12 × 12 × 8 = 12 × 96 = 48 m². Add: 48 + 48 = 96 m². The 10 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 11 × 6 = 66 cm². Triangle: base 18 − 11 = 7 cm, height 6 cm, so 12 × 7 × 6 = 12 × 42 = 21 cm². Add: 66 + 21 = 87 cm².

items.q: The dashed diagonal cuts the trapezoid into two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Bottom triangle: base 16 cm, height 8 cm: 12 × 16 × 8 = 12 × 128 = 64 cm². Top triangle: base 9 cm (the top side), same height: 12 × 9 × 8 = 12 × 72 = 36 cm². Add: 64 + 36 = 100 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the rhombus?
items.e: The diagonals cut the rhombus into 4 equal right triangles. It fills half of the 16 by 12 rectangle around it: 12 × 16 × 12 = 12 × 192 = 96 cm².

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 12 × 6 = 72 mm². The two triangles have the same height (6 mm), and their bases add up to 19 − 12 = 7 mm. Together: 12 × 7 × 6 = 12 × 42 = 21 mm². Add: 72 + 21 = 93 mm².

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 4 = 24 mm². The two triangles have the same height (4 mm), and their bases add up to 14 − 6 = 8 mm. Together: 12 × 8 × 4 = 12 × 32 = 16 mm². Add: 24 + 16 = 40 mm².

items.q: The horizontal diagonal cuts the kite into two triangles. What is the area of the kite?
items.e: Both triangles have the 15 mm diagonal as their base. Top: 12 × 15 × 4 = 12 × 60 = 30 mm². Bottom: 12 × 15 × 8 = 12 × 120 = 60 mm². Add: 30 + 60 = 90 mm².

items.q: What is the area of the rhombus?
items.e: The diagonals cut the rhombus into 4 equal right triangles. It fills half of the 18 by 8 rectangle around it: 12 × 18 × 8 = 12 × 144 = 72 mm².

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the trapezoid?
items.e: Rectangle 6 × 3 = 18 m², plus the two triangles together: 12 × 8 × 3 = 12 m² (their bases add up to 14 − 6 = 8 m). Total 30 m². The 5 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: The dashed diagonal cuts the trapezoid into two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Bottom triangle: base 13 m, height 6 m: 12 × 13 × 6 = 12 × 78 = 39 m². Top triangle: base 7 m (the top side), same height: 12 × 7 × 6 = 12 × 42 = 21 m². Add: 39 + 21 = 60 m².

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 10.5 cm and 5.5 cm. The distance between them (the height) is 7 cm. A diagonal cuts it into two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Each triangle has one of the parallel sides as its base and the same height. 12 × 10.5 × 7 = 12 × 73.5 = 36.75 and 12 × 5.5 × 7 = 12 × 38.5 = 19.25. Add: 36.75 + 19.25 = 56 cm².

items.q: The diagonals of the kite are 9 cm and 10 cm. What is its area?
items.e: The kite fits inside a rectangle that is 9 by 10 and fills exactly half of it (its two triangles are each half of a smaller rectangle). 12 × 9 × 10 = 12 × 90 = 45 cm².

items.q: A trapezoid has parallel sides of 12 m and 7.5 m. The distance between them (the height) is 4 m. A diagonal cuts it into two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Each triangle has one of the parallel sides as its base and the same height. 12 × 12 × 4 = 12 × 48 = 24 and 12 × 7.5 × 4 = 12 × 30 = 15. Add: 24 + 15 = 39 m².

items.q: The horizontal diagonal cuts the kite into two triangles. What is the area of the kite?
items.e: Both triangles have the 19 cm diagonal as their base. Top: 12 × 19 × 9 = 12 × 171 = 85.5 cm². Bottom: 12 × 19 × 13 = 12 × 247 = 123.5 cm². Add: 85.5 + 123.5 = 209 cm².

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 4 = 24 cm². The two triangles have the same height (4 cm), and their bases add up to 12 − 6 = 6 cm. Together: 12 × 6 × 4 = 12 × 24 = 12 cm². Add: 24 + 12 = 36 cm². The 5 cm side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: Which expression gives the area of the kite?
c: 12 × 12 × 4 + 12 × 12 × 9
items.e: Two triangles share the 12 cm diagonal as their base. Their heights are 4 cm and 9 cm. 12 × 12 × 4 + 12 × 12 × 9 = 24 + 54 = 78 cm². 12 × (4 + 9) forgets the 12.

items.q: The diagonals of the kite are 18 cm and 22 cm. What is its area?
items.e: The kite fits inside a rectangle that is 18 by 22 and fills exactly half of it (its two triangles are each half of a smaller rectangle). 12 × 18 × 22 = 12 × 396 = 198 cm².

items.q: The dashed lines cut the trapezoid into a rectangle and two triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 8 = 64 m². The two triangles have the same height (8 m), and their bases add up to 20 − 8 = 12 m. Together: 12 × 12 × 8 = 12 × 96 = 48 m². Add: 64 + 48 = 112 m². The 10 m side is slanted, so it is not the height.

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 7 − 4 = 3 cm tall. Rectangle: 6 × 4 = 24 cm². Triangle: 12 × 6 × 3 = 12 × 18 = 9 cm². Add: 24 + 9 = 33 cm².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: The triangle is 10 − 4 = 6 cm tall. Rectangle: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Triangle: 12 × 10 × 6 = 12 × 60 = 30 cm². Add: 40 + 30 = 70 cm².

items.q: The hexagon is a rectangle with two equal triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 7 × 8 = 56 mm². Each triangle: base 8 mm, height 5 mm, so 12 × 8 × 5 = 12 × 40 = 20 mm². Total: 56 + 20 + 20 = 96 mm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle 13 × 7 = 91, minus the missing corner 6 × 4 = 24: 91 − 24 = 67 mm². Or: split it into two rectangles: 7 × 7 = 49 and 6 × 3 = 18. Add: 49 + 18 = 67 mm².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 10 × 9 = 90 cm². The triangle’s base is 17 − 10 = 7 cm and its height is 9 cm: 12 × 7 × 9 = 12 × 63 = 31.5 cm². Add: 90 + 31.5 = 121.5 cm².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 11 × 8 = 88 cm². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 3 × 2 = 12 × 6 = 3 cm². Subtract: 88 − 3 = 85 cm².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into a rectangle and a triangle. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 9 × 4 = 36 m². The triangle’s base is 17 − 9 = 8 m and its height is 4 m: 12 × 8 × 4 = 12 × 32 = 16 m². Add: 36 + 16 = 52 m².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 10 × 10 = 100 mm². Triangle: its base is the 10 mm side and its height is 7 mm, so 12 × 10 × 7 = 12 × 70 = 35 mm². Add: 100 + 35 = 135 mm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 13 × 10 = 130 cm². Triangle: its base is the 10 cm side and its height is 6 cm, so 12 × 10 × 6 = 12 × 60 = 30 cm². Add: 130 + 30 = 160 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Rectangle: 14 × 10 = 140 cm². Triangle: its base is the 10 cm side and its height is 5 cm, so 12 × 10 × 5 = 12 × 50 = 25 cm². Add: 140 + 25 = 165 cm².

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 6 × 7 = 42 mm². Triangle: 12 × 6 × 3 = 12 × 18 = 9 mm². Add: 42 + 9 = 51 mm².

items.q: The hexagon is a rectangle with two equal triangles. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 9 × 8 = 72 m². Each triangle: base 8 m, height 4 m, so 12 × 8 × 4 = 12 × 32 = 16 m². Total: 72 + 16 + 16 = 104 m².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 4 × 7 = 28 and 6 × 3 = 18. Add: 28 + 18 = 46 m². Use each part of the figure once: 4 × 7 + 10 × 3 = 58 counts the 4 × 3 corner twice.

items.q: The figure is a rectangle with a triangle on top. What is its area?
items.e: Rectangle: 14 × 8 = 112 m². Triangle: 12 × 14 × 3 = 12 × 42 = 21 m². Add: 112 + 21 = 133 m².

items.q: What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle 13 × 7 = 91, minus the missing corner 7 × 4 = 28: 91 − 28 = 63 cm². Or: split it into two rectangles: 6 × 7 = 42 and 7 × 3 = 21. Add: 42 + 21 = 63 cm².

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 11 − 5 = 6 and 7 − 4 = 3. Whole rectangle 11 × 7 = 77, minus the missing corner 6 × 3 = 18: 77 − 18 = 59 m².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 11 × 7 = 77 cm². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 5 × 3 = 12 × 15 = 7.5 cm². Subtract: 77 − 7.5 = 69.5 cm².

items.q: The dashed line splits the figure into two rectangles. What is the area of the figure?
items.e: Split it into two rectangles: 5 × 9 = 45 and 6 × 5 = 30. Add: 45 + 30 = 75 cm². Use each part of the figure once: 5 × 9 + 11 × 5 = 100 counts the 5 × 5 corner twice.

items.q: What is the area of the figure? Find the two missing side lengths first.
items.e: Missing sides: 16 − 9 = 7 and 11 − 6 = 5. Whole rectangle 16 × 11 = 176, minus the missing corner 7 × 5 = 35: 176 − 35 = 141 cm².

items.q: A triangle is cut off the corner of a rectangle (grey dashed lines). What is the area of the shaded figure?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 13 × 6 = 78 m². Cut-off right triangle: 12 × 4 × 3 = 12 × 12 = 6 m². Subtract: 78 − 6 = 72 m².

sets.title: Word problems: gardens, sails and flags

items.q: A wooden sign is a rectangle 60 cm long and 20 cm tall with a triangle on one end, like an arrow. The triangle’s base is the 20 cm side, and it sticks out 15 cm. What is the area of the sign?
items.e: Rectangle: 60 × 20 = 1200 cm². Triangle: 12 × 20 × 15 = 12 × 300 = 150 cm². Total: 1200 + 150 = 1350 cm².

items.q: Students paint a mural on a wall shaped like a trapezoid. The parallel sides are 9 m and 7 m, and they are 5 m apart. One 1 L can of paint covers 10 m². How many cans do they need?
items.e: Cut it with a diagonal into two triangles: 12 × 9 × 5 = 22.5 m² and 12 × 7 × 5 = 17.5 m². Add: 22.5 + 17.5 = 40 m². Cans: 40 ÷ 10 = 4.

items.q: Olivia builds a kite. The two crossed sticks (the diagonals) are 60 cm and 80 cm long. How much paper covers the kite?
items.e: The kite fills half of the 60 cm by 80 cm rectangle around it: 12 × 60 × 80 = 12 × 4800 = 2400 cm².

items.q: A community garden shaped like a parallelogram has an area of 1200 m². Its base is 40 m. What is its height?
items.e: Area = base × height, so 40 × h = 1200. h = 1200 ÷ 40 = 30 m. (Halving is only for triangles.)

items.q: A garden bed at school is a trapezoid. Its parallel sides are 6 m and 4 m, and they are 3 m apart. What is its area?
items.e: Cut it with a diagonal into two triangles: 12 × 6 × 3 = 12 × 18 = 9 and 12 × 4 × 3 = 12 × 12 = 6. Add: 9 + 6 = 15 m².

items.q: A sailboat on Lake Ontario has a sail shaped like a right triangle. The bottom edge is 3 m, the edge along the mast is 4 m and the slanted edge is 5 m. What is the area of the sail?
items.e: The bottom edge and the mast meet at a right angle, so they are the base and the height. A = 12 × 3 × 4 = 12 × 12 = 6 m². The 5 m edge is slanted.

items.q: A backyard rink is an L-shape: a 12 m by 8 m rectangle with a 4 m by 3 m corner left out for a shed. What is the area of the ice?
items.e: Whole rectangle: 12 × 8 = 96 m². Corner: 4 × 3 = 12 m². Ice: 96 − 12 = 84 m².

items.q: A corner lot in Halifax is a right triangle. Its sides along the two streets are 30 m and 40 m, and the back side is 50 m. What is the area of the lot?
items.e: The two street sides meet at a right angle, so they are the base and the height. A = 12 × 30 × 40 = 12 × 1200 = 600 m². The 50 m side is slanted.

items.q: A parking space is a parallelogram. It is 2.5 m wide along the curb, and its painted slanted lines are 6 m long. The distance straight back from the curb is 5.5 m. What is its area?
items.e: A = base × height = 2.5 × 5.5 = 13.75 m². The 6 m lines are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: A park in Winnipeg is a rectangle 80 m long and 60 m wide. It has a triangular pond with a base of 20 m and a height of 15 m. The rest of the park is grass. What is the area of the grass?
items.e: Park: 80 × 60 = 4800 m². Pond: 12 × 20 × 15 = 12 × 300 = 150 m². Grass: 4800 − 150 = 4650 m².

items.q: A triangular sail has an area of 12 m². Its base is 4 m. How tall is the sail?
items.e: 12 × 4 × h = 12, so 4 × h = 24. h = 24 ÷ 4 = 6 m.

items.q: The front wall of a cottage is a rectangle 8 m wide and 3 m tall with a triangle on top that is 2 m tall. What is the area of the wall?
items.e: Rectangle: 8 × 3 = 24 m². Triangle: 12 × 8 × 2 = 12 × 16 = 8 m². Total: 24 + 8 = 32 m².

items.q: Zoe’s class makes 20 triangular flags for a Terry Fox Run banner. Each flag has a base of 30 cm and a height of 45 cm. How much fabric do the flags use in all?
items.e: One flag: 12 × 30 × 45 = 12 × 1350 = 675 cm². Twenty flags: 20 × 675 = 13 500 cm².

items.q: A triangular sail has sides of 10 m, 17 m and 21 m. The height to the 21 m side is 8 m. What is its area?
items.e: Use the 21 m side as the base and the 8 m height: A = 12 × 21 × 8 = 12 × 168 = 84 m². The 10 m and 17 m sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: A triangular flower bed has a base of 8 m and a height of 5 m. One packet of wildflower seeds covers 4 m². How many packets are needed for the whole bed?
items.e: Area: 12 × 8 × 5 = 12 × 40 = 20 m². Packets: 20 ÷ 4 = 5.

items.q: A team flag is a rectangle 90 cm long and 60 cm tall. A red triangle on the flag has the 60 cm side as its base and reaches 45 cm into the flag. The rest is white. What is the area of the white part?
items.e: Flag: 90 × 60 = 5400 cm². Triangle: 12 × 60 × 45 = 12 × 2700 = 1350 cm². White part: 5400 − 1350 = 4050 cm².

items.q: Arjun’s family plants a vegetable garden shaped like a parallelogram. Its base is 8 m and its height is 5 m. The slanted sides are 6 m long. What is the area of the garden?
items.e: A = base × height = 8 × 5 = 40 m². The 6 m sides are slanted, so they are not the height.

items.q: Owen’s family lays a path with 25 patio stones shaped like rhombuses. Each stone has diagonals of 40 cm and 30 cm. What area do the stones cover?
items.e: One stone: 12 × 40 × 30 = 12 × 1200 = 600 cm². 25 stones: 25 × 600 = 15 000 cm².

items.q: Aiden stains a deck shaped like a trapezoid. The parallel sides are 5 m and 3 m, and they are 4 m apart. Stain costs $6 per square metre. How much does the stain cost?
items.e: Cut it with a diagonal into two triangles: 12 × 5 × 4 = 10 m² and 12 × 3 × 4 = 6 m². Add: 10 + 6 = 16 m². Cost: 16 × $6 = $96.

items.q: Triangle A has a base of 10 cm and a height of 8 cm. Parallelogram B has a base of 5 cm and a height of 8 cm. Which is true?
c: A is twice as large as B.
items.e: A: 12 × 10 × 8 = 12 × 80 = 40 cm². B: 5 × 8 = 40 cm². Same area. (Forgetting the 12 makes A look twice as large.)
